newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mobutu family assets found in Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu family assets found in Swiss banks.

text.p: Swiss banks have found 4.8 million Swiss francs ($3.4 million) in assets held by former Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko or his family after a search ordered by the Berne government, authorities said on Tuesday.
The funds have been frozen in line with Berne's orders last month, the Federal Banking Commission said in a statement.

When Mobutu was toppled by rebels last month, the Swiss government ordered all banks in Switzerland to report whether they or their foreign subsidiaries were holding wealth for Mobutu, his family or their associates.

"All 406 banks answered on time. Six banks have reported such assets worth a total amount of 4,786,570.00 Swiss francs. These assets have been frozen on the basis of the Federal Council's decree of May 17, 1997" the banking watchdog said.
"The results of the survey largely confirm the result of an earlier survey by the FBC that was conducted at a few selected banks," it added.

The new government in Kinshasa has sought legal assistance from Berne in tracking down reports that Mobutu stashed billionS of dollars of looted national wealth abroad. In a newspaper interview last week, new Justice Minister Celestin Lwangi alleged Mobutu had put 11 billion Swiss francs in Switzerland.
